name: post-disaster-mobility-public
what_it_holds: Public-data pipeline linking FEMA National Risk Index (NRI), CDC Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), Census PUMA geographies, and FEMA disaster declarations through to IPUMS migration-PUMA level, i.e. models post-disaster population mobility/migration. Updated 15 Apr 2026, 'other' license.
why_useful: Post-disaster migration/mobility flows are a proxy for demand disruption and displacement travel (short-term-rental usage spikes for displaced residents) around hurricanes/wildfires, relevant to gap 11 and gap 20 (mobility/geospatial proxies).

name: nasa-wildfires
what_it_holds: LA Times Data Desk's Python tool to download wildfire hotspot detections from NASA satellites via FIRMS (MODIS/VIIRS), returning point-level fire-detection data with timestamps and confidence.
why_useful: A well-maintained (34 stars), newsroom-grade one-command puller for near-real-time and historical FIRMS hotspot data -- lower-fidelity than perimeter polygons but easy to script for any market/date range, including Hawaii and Southern California.
time_coverage: current NASA FIRMS archive (2000-present for MODIS, 2012-present VIIRS)

name: hurricaneexposuredata
what_it_holds: R data package with hazard-based exposure data (storm-level rain and wind exposure) for every US county within the Atlantic-basin hurricane-affected region, keyed to specific historical tropical-storm events; companion to the `hurricaneexposure` toolkit (rOpenSci-affiliated) which layers on visualization/analysis functions.
why_useful: County-level, storm-by-storm exposure intensity (not just track lines) lets you quantify how directly a given Inside Airbnb market (e.g. Florida, Gulf Coast, coastal NC/SC) was hit by a named storm -- useful for a hurricane-shock control variable in nights/ADR regressions, addressing gap #11.
time_coverage: historical tropical storms through package's last data refresh (package built off HURDAT2 vintages)

name: ibtracs
what_it_holds: Python API/wrapper for interfacing with NOAA's IBTrACS (International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship) global tropical-cyclone best-track dataset -- position, intensity, and metadata for every tracked tropical cyclone worldwide since ~1841 (satellite-era reliable from ~1980s).
why_useful: Global coverage (not just Atlantic/HURDAT2) matters for APAC typhoon exposure (Japan, Thailand, Philippines -- gap #7 APAC travel volume interacts with typhoon season) and for a global, not just US, hurricane/typhoon shock variable.
time_coverage: ~1841-present (reliable satellite era ~1980s-present), updated as NOAA IBTrACS releases new versions
size_hint: wrapper around NOAA's canonical IBTrACS CSV/NetCDF files (~10s of MB)
